rationale: This is essentially the published intangible-adjusted (and tangible-book) value ratio of the Eisfeldt–Kim–Papanikolaou / Peters–Taylor line of work, it is merely the already-evaluated value leg of PurgedBookValueDualFloors stripped of its screens, and as a raw unranked ratio it is non-monotonic wherever the reconstructed numerator turns negative.

A legitimate and internally consistent ablation that fills a genuinely empty cell (purged book × single floor) between two existing archive results, but it is a one-term deletion from the archive's best signal rather than new economics, so its value is diagnostic rather than exploratory.

This is a four-ingredient mechanical merge of two already-tested archive winners with arbitrary nested-SUMRANK weights and no new economic content; the "complementary measurement error" claim is untestable from the proposed construction and a win here would be uninterpretable overfitting.

A single, economically coherent lever on the archive's strongest signal — capitalizing advertising alongside R&D is the natural symmetric completion of the reconstruction — though the claim that coverage cost is nil is wrong in spirit, since xad is reported sparsely and COALESCE-to-zero makes brand capital a function of disclosure practice rather than economics, which the diagnosis should acknowledge.

Pairing the corrected book ratio with the never-before-matched allocation flow is a defensible new cell and usefully breaks the archive's dependence on TS_MIN floors, but the xrd+xad−dvc leg partially re-uses the same R&D dollars already inside the value numerator, so any gain will be hard to attribute cleanly.

The double-counting hypothesis is sharp, the expression matches it exactly, and it completes the 2x2 with the two existing dual-floor results, making this the most informative of the three ablations proposed here even though it is only a one-term change.
